questions.question: Higher What volume does 0.5 mol of chlorine gas occupy at RTP?
Higher How many moles are in 120 dm³ of neon gas at RTP?
Higher What mass of CO₂ (M r = 44) occupies 12 dm³ at RTP?
Higher In the reaction 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(g), what volume of oxygen is needed to react with 48 dm³ of hydrogen at RTP?

points.text: Mole ratio H₂ : O₂ = 2 : 1. Volume of O₂ = 48 ÷ 2 = 24 dm³

questions.question: Higher 4 g of methane (CH₄, M r = 16) is burned completely. Calculate the volume of CO₂ gas produced at RTP.

points.text: Moles of CH₄ = 4 ÷ 16 = 0.25 mol. From the equation, 1 mol CH₄ → 1 mol CO₂, so moles of CO₂ = 0.25 mol. Volume of CO₂ = 0.25 × 24 = 6 dm³

questions.question: Extended Answer 6 marks: Explain how to calculate gas volumes in reactions. <div class="

points.text: To calculate gas volumes, first write the balanced symbol equation and identify the mole ratio of gases. At RTP, 1 mole of any gas occupies 24 dm³, so the mole ratio equals the volume ratio. If you know the mass of a reactant, calculate moles (moles = mass ÷ M r ), then use the mole ratio to find moles of the gas, and multiply by 24 to find the volume in dm³. If you know the volume of a gas, calculate moles (moles = volume ÷ 24), use the mole ratio to find moles of the other gas, then convert back to volume. Only calculate gas volumes for gaseous substances — check state symbols carefully. Mar
